Bill detail (web)
f3-bill-detail-web · Pantopus house style v2 + addendum

Bill detail on web

A new web page for one bill, so every money notification, reminder and calendar row resolves to the exact bill: the amount, the due date and who marked it paid. Each artboard carries its name above the frame; artboards are drawn at 1× and scroll sideways inside their own frame on narrow screens.

All 27 artboards · batches 1–5 complete. Notes is the last artboard.

First the amount “$142.18” (h1, tabular figures), then “Due in 4 days · Fri 23 Oct” (h3, text.secondary) ending in the one StatusChip “Upcoming”, then the single primary “Mark paid”.
One semantic h1, “Clark Public Utilities, $142.18”: the provider is styled h2 and the amount h1 inside it. The ScopeChip “Your household” and “Maya and Sam can see this bill” sit under the provider: Jenna’s guest access (until Tue 20 Oct) means not everyone at the home can see bills, so the people are named.
Action row: “Mark paid” (primary.700), the text buttons “Paid a different amount” and “Skip this month”, and the overflow menu (Edit, Remove; Escape closes it). Right: the Details card, “Visible to: Maya and Sam”, reminders the day before and the day of.
Loop phase: no provenance block, no trend, and no empty slot where they will go. Back returns to the Bills list, restores its scroll and focuses this row, with no wash.

A second Mark paid · the race
Maya marked the bill paid on her phone at 6:02 PM, then pressed Mark paid on this page, which was still showing Upcoming. The server already has it: the page updates to “Paid” and the status line “Already marked paid by you on your phone · 6:02 PM” replaces the action row. No Undo here: this press changed nothing.
Nothing is sent twice: Sam gets one “marked paid” notification, from the phone’s write, when Maya leaves the phone’s bill screen.
If another person who can mark bills paid had got there first, the line would name them (“Already marked paid by <name> · 6:02 PM”). HOME A has no second such person, so only the phone case is drawn.

Greyscale verdicts · review aid, not published
  • Amount firstReads without colour: yes: size and weight carry the hierarchy — h1 amount, h3 due line, then one filled button.
  • StatusChipReads without colour: yes: a glyph and a word; Overdue adds the warning shape, never colour alone.
  • Primary vs secondaryReads without colour: yes: “Mark paid” is the only solid fill; the other actions are underlined text.
  • ScopeReads without colour: yes: the house glyph chip plus the sentence naming Maya and Sam.
  • LinksReads without colour: yes: every link and text button is underlined.

f3-bill-detail-web · web-1440 · 27-notes · light

Bill detail on web · Notes

Open questions, assumptions, deviations, invented strings and omitted states for f3-bill-detail-web (artboards 1–26).

Open questions

  • Letting members record “I paid this” is an open product decision. Today only Maya can mark bills paid; Sam sees “Maya can mark this paid.” (05).
  • The tick’s spoken name for other viewers is drawn as the fixed “you added this”, with the person in the row label (“October, 142 dollars 18 cents, added by Maya, you added this”). The Foundations legend overrides this if the two disagree.
  • StatusChip has no “Skipped” value, so the skipped state (15) shows no chip. Add one, or keep the chip absent while skipped?

Assumptions (from the brief)

  • Maya arrives from the Bills row; the reminder-row arrival is drawn only on Fri 23 Oct (06).
  • Skip affects one month; Remove affects the series.
  • Only-you bills never notify (08).
  • Due today is viewed on Fri 23 Oct.
  • The inventory’s “Already paid” is folded into “Mark paid”: one job, one button name, including on overdue bills (07).
  • Trend values come from the f10-bill-trend board; the trend error string is aligned to that board.
  • Detail uses the longer “Marked paid by” on purpose, per the “marked paid” glossary rule; Bills list rows keep the BillRow string “Paid by Maya”.
  • The visibility line names Maya and Sam while Jenna’s guest access lasts and switches to “Your household” after Tue 20 Oct.
  • The race pattern “Already marked paid by <name> · 6:02 PM” is for a future second person who can mark bills paid; not drawn, because HOME A has none (14).

Assumptions and deviations added by this board

  • Attached were the native Bills list (A08) and the mailbox item detail (A17). The web Bills list at 1440 and 390, the web Place tab with its sidebar, and the iOS bill detail were not; the sidebar, breadcrumb, topbar and Details card follow the house style and earlier web boards.
  • Trend: the reference-line label sits in a small key above the chart (dashed swatch + “Nearby average $127 · 14 homes”) so it never covers the columns; the line itself is unchanged. Only October carries the tick above its column. The water trend (13) scales to its own values, still zero-based.
  • At 390, Edit and Remove are stacked text buttons instead of the overflow menu.
  • A paid past month (13) shows no action row and no reminders; its due line is date only (“Due Fri 28 Aug”). Details there reads “Added by: Theo (no longer here), by hand”.
  • The race (14) shows a status line with no Undo, since that press changed nothing.
  • At 200% zoom (23) the sidebar becomes an icon rail with labels as accessible names; at 720 CSS px the action row still fits one line.
  • Worst case (22) is two labelled specimens in one frame: the longest provider, then the property-tax bill.
  • Dark (25, 26): the one-time highlight would use surface.raised as its wash (Foundations D1); the Paid chip and the InlineUndo line sit on dark base and raised surfaces.

  • Account 4417, NW Natural, State Farm, Theo, the August water amounts, $120.00, 6:02 PM, the Sun 22 Nov and Mon 23 Nov reminder dates, “Maya and Sam can see this bill”, “This removes the monthly bill and its future months.”, and the other-viewer provenance and trend captions.

  • The bill edit form (Edit opens the existing form).
  • Also not drawn as frames: the overflow menu open, Escape closing it, the Bills list with the restored row focus, the grouped “Maya marked 3 bills paid” landing on the list, the Today strip and Mail arrivals (phase 2), and the trend’s cold-load skeleton and error states.
